Chest X-Ray Classification: Pneumonia and Normal¶

Project Done By Jackelyn Valencia

Description of Dataset¶

  • This dataset contains chest x-ray images, where some are classified as "pneumonia" and the rest as "normal".
  • The dataset is split into two different sets: one called "Train" and the other called "Test". We will be using these sets to train and test some algorithms that we will use later on
    • The train set contains a total of 5216 images (1341 normal, 3875 pneumonia)
    • The test set contains a total of ...

maybe analysis for checkpoint 2¶

  • Train: total of 5216 (1341 normal, 3875 pneumonia)
  • Already normalized since its grayscale images
  • Based on the explained_variance, answer if a low number of principal components explains most of the variance.
    • depends, for me, I needed to use a higher number so that i can explain more variance from the images

In [6]:
def process_img(image_path, is_grayscale=False, img_size=100):
    img = cv2.imread(image_path)
    if is_grayscale:
        img = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY)
    img = cv2.resize(img, (img_size, img_size))
    img = img.astype('float') / 255
    img = img.flatten()
    img = pd.Series(img)
    return img
In [7]:
def process_image_set(cols, type_xray, is_grayscale=False, img_size=100):
    start = time.time()
    cols = np.arange(cols)
    df = pd.DataFrame(columns=cols)
    labelcol = []
    x = 0
    for subdir, _, files in os.walk(raw_data):
        for file in files:
            img_path = subdir + os.sep + file
            img = process_img(img_path, is_grayscale, img_size)
            df.loc[x] = img
            x += 1
            labelcol.append(type_xray)
    df['label'] = labelcol
    print("Dataset finished processing")
    end = time.time()
    print(f"Time elapsed: {end - start}")
    return df

def plot_gallery(title, images, n_col=n_col, n_row=n_row, cmap=plt.cm.gray):
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(
        nrows=n_row,
        ncols=n_col,
        figsize=(2.0 * n_col, 2.3 * n_row),
        facecolor="white",
        constrained_layout=True,
    )
    fig.set_constrained_layout_pads(w_pad=0.01, h_pad=0.02, hspace=0, wspace=0)
    fig.set_edgecolor("black")
    fig.suptitle(title, size=16)
    for ax, vec in zip(axs.flat, images):
        vmax = max(vec.max(), -vec.min())
        im = ax.imshow(
            vec.reshape(image_shape),
            cmap=cmap,
            interpolation="nearest",
            vmin=-vmax,
            vmax=vmax,
        )
        ax.axis("off")

    fig.colorbar(im, ax=axs, orientation="horizontal", shrink=0.99, aspect=40, pad=0.01)
    plt.show()

In [ ]:
# self:
# data: train_data
# path: train_path
# transform: train_transform

class X_rayDataset:
    def __init__(self, data, path , transform = None):
        super().__init__()
        self.data = data.values
        self.path = path
        self.transform = transform
        
    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.data)
    
    def __getitem__(self,index):
        img_name,label = self.data[index]
        img_path = os.path.join(self.path, img_name)
        image = img.imread(img_path)
        if self.transform is not None:
            image = self.transform(image)
        return image, label

import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(3, 6, 5)
        self.pool = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(6, 16, 5)
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(16 * 5 * 5, 120)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(120, 84)
        self.fc3 = nn.Linear(84, 10)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.pool(F.relu(self.conv1(x)))
        x = self.pool(F.relu(self.conv2(x)))
        x = torch.flatten(x, 1) # flatten all dimensions except batch
        x = F.relu(self.fc1(x))
        x = F.relu(self.fc2(x))
        x = self.fc3(x)
        return x


net = Net()
In [ ]:
import torch.optim as optim

criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = optim.SGD(net.parameters(), lr=0.001, momentum=0.9)
In [ ]:
for epoch in range(2):  # loop over the dataset multiple times

    running_loss = 0.0
    for i, data in enumerate(trainloader, 0):
        # get the inputs; data is a list of [inputs, labels]
        inputs, labels = data

        # zero the parameter gradients
        optimizer.zero_grad()

        # forward + backward + optimize
        outputs = net(inputs)
        loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()

        # print statistics
        running_loss += loss.item()
        if i % 2000 == 1999:    # print every 2000 mini-batches
            print(f'[{epoch + 1}, {i + 1:5d}] loss: {running_loss / 2000:.3f}')
            running_loss = 0.0

print('Finished Training')

# custom dataloader using Pytorch
# pass the path to the dataset directory, image transformations, and determine whether the dataset
# is being used for training or testing

# class xrayDataset(Dataset)
class xrayDataset():
    
    # __init__ method
    # My notes: defines the class variables and the image transformations
    # and defines two vaiables "self.images" and "self.labels". Tjeu willl
    # be read later (the images and labels) and store them here
    def __init__(self,root, train = False, transforms = None):
        
        self.root = root
        print(self.root)
        self.transforms = transforms
        print(self.transforms)
        self.train = train
        print(self.train)
        
        self.train_data = []
        for dirname, _, filenames in os.walk('C:/Users/DellDepot/Downloads/chest_xray/train/NORMAL'):
            for filename in filenames:
                print(os.path.join(dirname, filename))
                image2 = os.path.join(dirname, filename)
                self.train_data.append(image2)
        print("self.train_data:", self.train_data)
        self.test_data = [file for file in os.listdir(root) if "test" in file]
        
        self.data_files = self.train_data if self.train else self.test_data
        self.images = []
        self.labels = []
        
        self.load_data()
        
    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.images)
    
    def __getitem__(self,idx):
        
        if torch.is_tensor(idx):
            idx = idx.tolist()
            
        image = self.images[idx]
        image = Image.fromarray(image)
        
        label = self.labels[idx]
        
        if self.transforms:
            image = self.transforms(image)
            
        return image, label
    
    # fix this
    def load_data(self):
        
        print("this is self.data_files in load_data()", self.data_files)
        for file in self.data_files:
            print("this is file in load function:",file)
            file_path = os.path.join(self.root, file)
            sample = self.read_file(file_path)
            self.images.append(sample["data"])
            self.labels.extend(sample["labels"])

        print(self.images)
        self.images = np.vstack(self.images).reshape(-1, 3, 32, 32)
        self.images = self.images.transpose((0, 2, 3, 1))

    def read_file(self, filename):
        with open(filename, "rb") as f:
            f = pickle.loads(f)
        return f

import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(3, 6, 5)
        self.pool = nn.MaxPool2d(2, 2)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(6, 16, 5)
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(16 * 100 * 100, 100 * 100) # 400 by 120
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(100 * 100, 1600) # 120 by 84
        self.fc3 = nn.Linear(1600, 2) #84 by 10

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.pool(F.relu(self.conv1(x)))
        x = self.pool(F.relu(self.conv2(x)))
        x = torch.flatten(x, 1) # flatten all dimensions except batch
        x = F.relu(self.fc1(x))
        x = F.relu(self.fc2(x))
        x = self.fc3(x)
        return x


net = Net()
